title: GUIDE — 0. Architecture
content:
## 0. Architecture

```
crawl_sarvam.py        → docs/            (resume-safe crawl: sitemap + llms.txt + subdomains)
update_incremental.py  → incremental pass (new + lastmod-stale only)
sarvam-crawl.service   → systemd, Restart=on-failure
sarvam-update.timer    → daily 06:30 UTC incremental (VM-side; no GitHub Actions per project decision)
```

Stack: **Scrapling → Crawl4AI → ScrapeGraphAI → httpx** fallback chain (same `fetch_one` pattern as every repo in this family); docs saved as frontmatter `.md` + `_meta/*.json` + `_index.jsonl` + `_manifest.json`; state in `crawl_state.json`.

section: Phase 0 — Read the docs (source of truth)
content:
## Phase 0 — Read the docs (source of truth)

Base: `/data/opencode/sarvam/` — a full crawl of `https://docs.sarvam.ai/` (1090 pages, `docs/`).

1. `docs/README` + `guide_code/README.md` → understood crawl layout.
2. `docs/creative-text-to-speech.md`, `creative-tts-generate.md`, `creative-tts-best-practices.md` → Content-Studio UI docs (dashboard, not API — noted and set aside).
3. `docs/api-reference/text-to-speech/convert.md` → the real contract: `POST https://api.sarvam.ai/text-to-speech`, header `api-subscription-key`, body `{text (≤2500), language_code/speaker/pace/pitch/loudness/speech_sample_rate/enable_preprocessing/model/output_audio_codec/temperature/dict_id}`, response `{request_id, audios:[base64]}`.
4. `docs/api-reference/authentication.md` → auth header; failures are **403**, not 401.
5. `docs/api/api-guides-tutorials/text-to-speech/voices.md` → Tamil shortlist; `best-practices.md` (v4 Flash guide) → punctuation table, preprocessing, chunking, 48 kHz REST, pitch/loudness on v4.
6. Grep for `ta-IN` across `docs/` → confirmed language code + Tamil-capable speakers.

title: HOW_IT_WAS_DONE — Phase 1 — Live-verify every claim (trust, then verify)
section: Phase 1 — Live-verify every claim (trust, then verify)
content:
## Phase 1 — Live-verify every claim (trust, then verify)

Docs contradicted each other (reference page: pitch/loudness v2-only; v4 guide: supported on v4; `vetri_*` vs `aravind_*` Tamil names). Each was settled with a tiny live call before building on it:

```bash
# 1. Tamil voices that actually work
python3 -c "… POST … speaker=vetri_ta_suspense …"   # → 400, live list has aravind_ta_*
python3 -c "… speaker=aravind_ta_suspense, model=bulbul:v4-flash …"  # → 200 OK
python3 -c "… speaker=rohan / ishita, model=bulbul:v3 …"             # → 200 OK
# 2. Full v4 roster: sent speaker=xxx, parsed 400 error → 224 IDs, 4 Tamil, all male
# 3. Speech rate: 180 Tamil chars → 13.95 s ⇒ ~770 chars/min ⇒ ~23,000 chars ≈ 30 min
# 4. v4 extras: pitch −0.1 + loudness 1.1 + enable_preprocessing + 44100 Hz → 200 OK (reference page was stale)
```

Findings locked in: `target_language_code: ta-IN`; v4 Tamil = 4 male IDs; v3 needed for female; ~770 chars/min; pitch/loudness/preprocessing/44.1 kHz all live on v4.

title: HOW_IT_WAS_DONE — Phase 2 — Half-hour thriller (single voice, v4)
content:
## Phase 2 — Half-hour thriller (single voice, v4)

1. Authored `tamil_thriller_story.txt` (~28,199 chars, 10 chapters, Rajesh Kumar style: DSP Vivek, locked room, 2nd murder, twist + open ending) in 3 appended parts.
2. `generate_tts.py`: sentence-boundary chunks (~1900 chars, 15 chunks) → per-chunk POST (`aravind_ta_suspense`, pace 0.92, 22050 Hz mp3) with retries + skip-existing resume → base64-decode → `ffmpeg -f concat -safe 0 -c copy` → `ffprobe` verify.
3. Result: `tamil_thriller_half_hour.mp3`, 2214 s = **36.9 min**. Ran as background job (~15 chunks).

```bash
export SARVAM_API_KEY="உங்கள்_கீ"
curl -X POST https://api.sarvam.ai/text-to-speech \
  -H "api-subscription-key: $SARVAM_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "text": "வணக்கம்! இன்று நாம் ஏஐ பற்றிப் பேசுவோம்.",
    "target_language_code": "ta-IN",
    "speaker": "vijay_ta_narration",
    "model": "bulbul:v4-flash",
    "pace": 1.0,
    "speech_sample_rate": 22050,
    "output_audio_codec": "mp3"
  }' -o பதில்.json
# பதில்: {"request_id":"…","audios":["<base64>"]} → base64-ஐ டிகோட் செய்து mp3 ஆக்கவும்

Python-இல்:

```python
import json, base64, urllib.request
def tts(text, speaker="vijay_ta_narration", model="bulbul:v4-flash", pace=1.0, key="YOUR_KEY"):
    payload = {"text": text, "target_language_code": "ta-IN", "speaker": speaker,
               "model": model, "pace": pace, "speech_sample_rate": 22050,
               "output_audio_codec": "mp3"}
    req = urllib.request.Request("https://api.sarvam.ai/text-to-speech",
        data=json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8"),
        headers={"api-subscription-key": key, "Content-Type": "application/json"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=120) as r:
        return base64.b64decode(json.loads(r.read())["audios"][0])
open("/tmp/வணக்கம்.mp3", "wb").write(tts("வணக்கம் மக்களே!"))
```

| குரல் | பாணி | எதற்கு |

| `aravind_ta_suspense` | சஸ்பென்ஸ் | திரில்லர், கிரைம் கதை |
| `vijay_ta_narration` | விவரிப்பு | ஆடியோபுக், செய்தி, கல்வி |

title: Authentication — Bearer token (alternative)
content:
### Bearer token (alternative)

The API also accepts the same key as a standard `Authorization: Bearer` header on all endpoints:
    
    
    Authorization: Bearer YOUR_SARVAM_API_KEY

This is useful with OpenAI-compatible tooling pointed at the [Chat Completions endpoint](https://docs.sarvam.ai/api/api-guides-tutorials/chat-completion/overview) (`/v1/chat/completions`), which conventionally sends Bearer auth. All examples in these docs and the official SDKs use the `api-subscription-key` header. Prefer it unless your tooling requires Bearer.

title: Authentication — Obtaining Your API Subscription Key
content:
### Obtaining Your API Subscription Key

  1. **Sign Up** : Create an account on the [Sarvam Dashboard](https://dashboard.sarvam.ai/)
  2. **Generate Key** : After signing up, you must manually generate your API key from the dashboard. Navigate to the API Keys section and create a new key for your account.
  3. **Organisation Key Management** : Creating Organisational level keys is not currently supported and will be available soon.

**Save your key value right away.** For security reasons, the value of a previously created API key can’t be retrieved again after you navigate away, the dashboard only ever shows it once, at creation time.

If you lose a key’s value or believe it’s been misused, delete the key from the dashboard and generate a new one. Copy and save the new key’s value immediately, since it won’t be accessible afterwards either.

#### Best Practices for API Key Management

This page is for Model APIs.

The `reasoning_effort` parameter controls **how much effort the model puts into reasoning and planning its response**.

  * Higher effort → more thoughtful, step-by-step, or structured answers
  * Lower effort → faster, simpler replies

* * *

title: How to adjust the model's thinking level with reasoning_effort — Allowed values:
content:
### Allowed values:

**Value**| **Behavior**  
---|---  
`"low"`| Quick, simple replies  
`"medium"`| Balanced depth and speed (**default value**)  
`"high"`| More detailed reasoning and structured answers  
`None`| Disables reasoning completely  
  
* * *

title: How to adjust the model's thinking level with reasoning_effort — 💡 Tips:
content:
### 💡 Tips:

  * Use `"low"` when you want **short, direct responses**.
  * Use `"medium"` for **balanced performance** (this is the default).
  * Use `"high"` for tasks like **explanations, problem solving, reasoning**.
  * Use `None` to **completely disable reasoning** when you want the fastest possible responses.

**Note:**

  * Setting higher reasoning effort may **increase response time** slightly, since the model is thinking more.

    from sarvamai import SarvamAI

# How to control response diversity with top_p | Sarvam API Docs

> Source: https://docs.sarvam.ai/api/api-guides-tutorials/chat-completion/how-to/control-response-diversity/

[API Guides & Tutorials](https://docs.sarvam.ai/api/api-guides-tutorials/chat-completion/overview)[Large Language Models](https://docs.sarvam.ai/api/api-guides-tutorials/chat-completion/overview)[How-to](https://docs.sarvam.ai/api/api-guides-tutorials/chat-completion/how-to/list-your-chat-messages)

# 

How to control response diversity with `top_p`

This page is for Model APIs.

The `top_p` parameter controls **how much of the probability space** the model uses when selecting the next word. This is called **nucleus sampling**.

**Range:** `0` to `1`  
**Default:** `1.0`

  * Lower `top_p` → model chooses from a **smaller set of highly likely words** → more focused
  * Higher `top_p` → model chooses from a **broader set of words** → more diverse

* * *

This page is for Model APIs.

The `top_p` parameter controls **how much of the probability space** the model uses when selecting the next word. This is called **nucleus sampling**.

**Range:** `0` to `1`  
**Default:** `1.0`

  * Lower `top_p` → model chooses from a **smaller set of highly likely words** → more focused
  * Higher `top_p` → model chooses from a **broader set of words** → more diverse

title: How to control response diversity with top_p — When to use:
content:
### When to use:

**`top_p` value**| **Behavior**  
---|---  
`0.1`| Very focused, only top 10% words used  
`0.3`| Controlled diversity  
`0.5`| Balanced creativity and accuracy  
`0.8 - 1.0`| Very creative, open-ended responses  
`1.0` (default)| Full probability space used  
  
First, install the SDK:
    
    
    pip install -Uqq sarvamai

Then use the following Python code:

# 

How to control response randomness with `temperature`

This page is for Model APIs.

The `temperature` parameter controls how **focused or varied** model responses are.

**Range:** `0` to `2`  
**Default:** `0.2`

  * **Lower temperature** → more focused, predictable answers (e.g. `0.2`)
  * **Higher temperature** → more creative, varied responses (e.g. `0.8` or `1.0`)

👉 **Tip** : For most use cases, values between `0.2` and `0.8` give good results.

Output is not bit-reproducible, even with `temperature=0`. Use a lower temperature to reduce variation, not to guarantee identical responses.

# 

How to control where the model stops using `stop`

This page is for Model APIs.

The `stop` parameter lets you define **one or more strings** that tell the model to **stop generating further tokens** when it encounters them.

  * The stop sequence(s) will **not appear** in the returned text.
  * `stop` is a **hard stop** : the model will not generate anything past the stop string.
  * You can use `stop` to: 
    * **Format structured outputs**
    * Avoid responses that **run too long**
    * Segment **multi-part answers**
